1: This freeze authorizes only the oracle package. Section 6 records prospective neural design commitments and does not constitute an executable inference protocol. No checkpoint is opened. The later inference specification must be reviewed and frozen before checkpoint inspection, including its absolute response-magnitude floor and complete numerical and outcome-accounting rules.
2: Use p for the four-state probability vector and theta=(mu_x,mu_y,kappa) for its chart. Phi(p,u) is a ratio of linear functions of p. Chart perturbations mean p'=inverse_chart(theta(p)+Delta). In O5, 'kappa zeroed' means setting the kappa component of Delta to zero while retaining the recipient's baseline kappa. The O5 contrast is descriptive and is not assigned an H*sin^2(theta) interpretation without a derivation for its exact target and weighting.
3: Fit B and B_mu by weighted least squares using ALL output components, fitting-prefix law weights and all continuations. Use the same fitted maps for ALL, MARG and XOR reporting. B_mu has its kappa row fixed to zero; neither fit is constrained to attain a specified rank. The minimum-norm solution convention and numerical solver are frozen in the manifest. O6's predicted-response identity is checked componentwise to maximum absolute error 1e-9 on valid edits.
4: For O6 and O7, an edit is scoreable only when the control's actual perturbed belief and both predicted perturbed beliefs satisfy the declared probability guard. Both models and response energy use exactly the same scoreable-edit mask. Invalid edits are not assigned zero error and are never replaced. Report raw-count and law-mass coverage for every fold and size. The oracle reference requires at least 75% coverage by both measures in every fold.
5: Pool evaluated occurrences using their original w(a,u), with equal direction and sign weights, and normalize once over the pooled scoreable occurrences. Do not average separately normalized fold losses. With complete coverage, each history occurs in three evaluation folds, giving denominator three times total history mass, apart from the uniform edit factor. With incomplete coverage, report the retained mass and state that losses are conditional on the common scoreable-edit subset. H*, response energy and their ratio use identical masks and weights.
6: O7 is an exploratory restricted-comparator fixture, not a required behavioral negative control. Specify the polynomial basis, coefficient normalization and minimum-norm fitting convention for g. Evaluate its derivatives and finite predictions about its own baseline chart (mu_x,mu_y,g(mu_x,mu_y)); report disagreement with the true reachable oracle separately. Check baseline belief validity before derivative evaluation. Failure of the quadratic to define a valid baseline is reported as RESTRICTED COMPARATOR NOT ADMISSIBLE, not automatically as PIPELINE INVALID. It does not trigger refitting or replacement.
7: O7's two-coordinate construction implies Jacobian rank at most two. Exact rank two requires a separate argument for the specified outputs and domain. Resolved lower rank is reported, not automatically treated as an implementation failure. A resolved third direction contradicts the fixture's structural construction and requires an integrity diagnosis. Numerical ambiguity is reported as unresolved.
8: The rank rule includes equality cases in the unresolved band. An identically zero singular spectrum has numerical rank zero without forming sigma_i/sigma_1. Report sigma_1 as well as relative singular values; relative rank is not a sensitivity measure. Freeze the treatment of zero response energy and numerical boundary cases before execution. Undefined ratios are not replaced by zero or counted as passing thresholds.
9: H* is the synthetic comparator loss and ideal improvement headroom when the full synthetic predictor is exact. Report the actual measured gain separately. For a neural checkpoint, L_mu is an upper bound on possible squared-error improvement, not a guarantee of attainable gain. The condition L_full<=L_mu/2 concerns total comparator prediction error and is not interpreted as a bound on a separately identified kappa-error component.
10: The prospective neural substantive-headroom condition is pooled L_mu/S>=0.02 for each counted size and output group. It is a declared relative-effect convention. Together with halving L_mu it requires improvement of at least 0.01*S. A separate absolute response-magnitude floor remains required before inference. Foldwise headroom is reported but does not independently determine the seed's headroom status.
11: For each output group, report disjoint seed counts p, f, u and h for PASS, verified FAIL, UNRESOLVED and HEADROOM NOT MET. More than two unresolved seeds gives UNRESOLVED; otherwise more than two headroom-limited seeds gives HEADROOM NOT MET; otherwise more than two combined gives UNRESOLVED for insufficient evaluable seeds. With those checks satisfied, p>=8 gives POSITIVE. NOT SHOWN requires p+u+h<=2. MIXED requires 3<=p and p+u+h<8. Remaining cases are UNRESOLVED because unavailable comparisons can change the outcome category. No unavailable comparison is counted as verified failure.
12: The counted neural edit magnitudes are finite intervention commitments, not proof of nonlinearity. Report actual finite responses, Jacobian predictions and their discrepancy at every declared size. Agreement in a linear regime is not counted as independent mechanistic replication of the Jacobian fit. No magnitude is substituted after inspection.
13: Step 0 performs O1 and O2 before sampling O6 work. The first 1,000 sampled O6 propagations are retained and not recomputed for timing. Remaining propagation counts use frozen scheduled upper counts with completed work subtracted. The projection is a heuristic that omits or separately estimates non-propagation overhead; it is not a runtime bound. A projection-triggered stop is distinguished from reaching the hard cap.
14: The cumulative wall-clock interval starts before interpreter imports and setup and includes final serialization and report writing. Enforce the ten-minute limit independently of the throughput projection. Preserve completed outputs on stopping. The pre-execution manifest is immutable; output hashes and run accounting are written to a separate post-run index referencing that manifest.
